survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note is a governance and responsibilities mapping for Denmark’s adult skills system and does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA assessment. As a result, there is no sampling frame, no student-level analytic dataset, and no application of complex survey weights or replicate-weight procedures. The tables describe institutional roles (national/regional/local) and expenditure shares rather than estimating achievement or learning outcomes. For this type of report, weighting guidance is not applicable because there are no PV-based scales, no student responses, and no statistical model requiring survey-weighted estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document does not use ILSA-style cognitive achievement outcomes with Plausible Values; it is a policy/governance description of adult skills system responsibilities and expenditure structure. Because there is no student-level assessment dataset and no PV-based scoring, missing-data handling for PVs is not part of the analysis. The tables are based on institutional and administrative information compiled by the OECD rather than on respondent-level test data.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No student-level sample is constructed. The note focuses on Denmark’s adult skills system governance structure and summarizes responsibilities across national, regional, and local levels using OECD compilation sources.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Denmark country note provides an overview of how the adult skills system is governed, focusing on the allocation of responsibilities across national, regional, and local levels. It describes which ministries oversee VET, HVET, CET, adult education (AE), and Active Labour Market Policies (ALMPs), and how implementation is carried out by municipalities, independent VET schools, adult education and training centres, and regional bodies. The report includes governance/expenditure structure information (e.g., the share of general government expenditure at sub-national level) and responsibility matrices indicating strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, and delivery roles by policy area. Because it is not an assessment of student performance, it does not use ILSA-style instruments, plausible values, or statistical scaling. Consequently, there are no ML models, predictive metrics, or achievement benchmarks; the “results” are institutional arrangements and policy design features relevant for adult-skills governance.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a non-empirical policy country note that compiles governance information rather than conducting an ILSA-based student outcome analysis. Therefore, fields that normally require an analytic sample, PV handling, missing-data strategy, and ML model evaluation are not populated. The extraction is intentionally sparse because the document does not report student-level data, model-based results, or quantitative achievement benchmarks.
